tags.hand:about: A Duffey classic: a tree tour up the northwest shoulder of Joffre Peak, in Baldwin's guidebook. Old-growth forest skiing up to about 1,900 m, then a short climb onto open slopes to the shoulder at about 2,200 m. Skiers pick it on powder days when the alpine avalanche danger is high, because most of it stays in the trees (but steep slopes still rise above parts of the forest). Ski laps in the forest, or the open slopes near the top.
tags.hand:climb: About 960 m over 4.7 km one way (3 to 4 hours up)
tags.hand:start: Cayoosh weather station pull-out on Highway 99 (Duffey Lake Road), about 2.5 km past the Joffre Lakes parking toward Lillooet. Head south into the trees. You can also start from the Joffre Lakes lot.
tags.hand:safety: There are bluffs low in the forest: keep to the climber's left of them. Slopes in the trees reach about 30°. Above the shoulder the ridge steepens onto Joffre Peak's avalanche and glacier terrain, so turn around there unless the snow is stable and you know the terrain. Below about 1,500 m the snow can be thin early in the season (slide alder).
tags.hand:rules: Part of the route is in Joffre Lakes Park (Pipi7íyekw), run with the Lil'wat and N'Quatqua Nations: check bcparks.ca for closures before you go.
tags.hand:line: Drawn from the trip reports and the terrain model (the easiest way up the shoulder), not a GPS track: follow the skin track and your own judgment.

tags.hand:aka: Chief Pascal, Pascall
tags.hand:about: A Duffey classic and a good first Duffey peak: an old spur road, then a steep skin track through mature forest to open slopes and the northwest ridge, then up its southwest side to the summit at about 2,200 m (a boulder you go round the back of and climb onto), with views of the Joffre group. Lots of lines off the ridge between about 2,000 and 2,100 m: the north face and bowl, and the north-facing glades lower down.
tags.hand:climb: About 940 m over 5.3 km one way (about 4 hours up)
tags.hand:high: About 2,200 m (the summit); most people drop in from the ridge at 2,000 to 2,100 m
tags.hand:start: Cayoosh weather station pull-out on Highway 99 (Duffey Lake Road), shortly past the Joffre Lakes parking toward Lillooet, the same lot as Joffre Shoulder. Follow the skin track into the forest, along a flat old road, then up through the trees and the cutblock. You can also come up the west ridge glades from the Cerise Creek lot.
tags.hand:safety: The north face reaches about 40° near the top and there is a couloir on the northeast face: avalanche terrain above the trees. The last bit along the ridge to the summit is steep. The cutblock snow can be poor (crust under new snow) and the exit is through tight trees.
tags.hand:line: Follows a skier's GPS track from March 2026 (tareef.tech, the link below), simplified, up to the summit, on the old spur road (the usual winter way in).

tags.hand:aka: Kayoosh, Cayoosh, Armchair Glacier, Lazy Boy, Ottoman
tags.hand:about: The big Duffey classic: up Cayoosh Creek past Cayoosh Cabin, the Ottoman slide path and a small lake at about 1,800 m, then the Armchair Glacier to the col at about 2,400 m under Cayoosh Mountain (2,561 m). Ski the glacier back down, or the north glacier from the col. The Lazy Boy bowls (south and southeast) are off the same approach.
tags.hand:climb: About 1,250 m over 8.5 km one way to the col (5 to 6 hours up); about 1,400 m and 18 km return with the summit
tags.hand:high: About 2,400 m (the Armchair col); the summit is 2,561 m, a short steep bootpack above the col
tags.hand:aspect: East (the Armchair Glacier), north (the north glacier)
tags.hand:start: Marriott Basin trailhead on Highway 99 (Duffey Lake Road), about 1 km past the Cayoosh weather station pull-out toward Lillooet. Follow the Cayoosh Creek forest road north for about 2.5 km, then the forest trail west past Cayoosh Cabin.
tags.hand:safety: Glacier travel: crevasses (more on the north glacier's skier's right). The approach crosses the Ottoman and other big slide paths under steep slopes: don't stop in them. The summit ridge is steep, firm and exposed (crampons and an ice axe help). The Million Dollar Couloir has cliffs at its entrance. Afternoon sun bakes the east slopes.
tags.hand:line: Drawn from the trip reports and the terrain model (Cayoosh Creek road, Cayoosh Cabin, the lake at about 1,800 m, the Armchair Glacier to the col), not a GPS track: follow the skin track and your own judgment.

tags.hand:about: The main way into the Sky Pilot backcountry from the gondola: along the Backcountry Access Road, then up the Habrich Spur logging road and the Sky Pilot Valley trail into the basin under Mount Habrich's south face and the Stadium Glacier. From the basin: Stadium Gully, Co-Pilot Gully, CMA, Hot Dog, Exit Gully off Habrich and the couloirs of the Ledge. Sky Pilot's summit itself is a mountaineering climb (glacier, exposed rock), not a ski.
tags.hand:climb: About 520 m over 5.4 km one way to the basin (2 to 3 hours up); add 300 to 700 m for laps. Sky Pilot's West Ridge plus a Co-Pilot lap makes a big day of about 1,500 m and 10 km.
tags.hand:high: About 1,350 m at the basin; the bowls above go to about 1,900 m (Co-Pilot) and 2,030 m (Sky Pilot)
tags.hand:aspect: Mostly north and west-facing slopes above the basin
tags.hand:start: Ride the Sea to Sky Gondola (Squamish, Highway 99) to the Summit Lodge at 885 m. Skis and boards go up only with backcountry gear, and not when Avalanche Canada's South Coast forecast is High or Extreme. Follow the groomed Backcountry Access Road (Shannon Creek Road) from the lodge.
tags.hand:safety: Complex avalanche terrain: big slopes, gullies and couloirs, cornices on the ridges, and the Stadium Glacier (crevasses). Above the end of the logging road there is no marked trail in winter. Not for beginners: the gondola says this is no place to learn.
tags.hand:rules: The gondola gets you up; past its maintained area nothing is controlled, marked or patrolled. Know the last ride down and be back well before it: if weather stops the gondola early you ski down the service road. Emergency: 911, then the gondola's line 604-892-2555.
tags.hand:groomed: The first 2.2 km (Backcountry Access Road) is groomed every day in winter
tags.hand:line: Follows the summer trails mapped on OpenStreetMap (access road, Habrich Spur, Sky Pilot Valley trail); the winter skin track can go elsewhere.

tags.hand:about: The centre ridge of the upper Shannon Creek watershed, from the end of the Backcountry Access Road straight up to the alpine between Sky Pilot and Goat Ridge, with views of Goat Ridge, Mount Habrich and the Sky Pilot group. Reaches the Goat Ridge lines (Goat Approach, Goat Couloir, Chamois Chute, Skinny Tree) and the Saddle and Co-Face slopes.
tags.hand:climb: About 700 to 800 m over 8.8 km one way (4 to 5 hours up); the summer trail is 17.8 km return
tags.hand:high: About 1,550 m where the trail ends in the alpine
tags.hand:aspect: Ridge; slopes off it face north and east
tags.hand:start: Ride the Sea to Sky Gondola (Squamish, Highway 99) to the Summit Lodge at 885 m. Skis and boards go up only with backcountry gear, and not when Avalanche Canada's South Coast forecast is High or Extreme. Follow the groomed Backcountry Access Road (Shannon Creek Road) from the lodge. Turn right at the end of the road and cross Shannon Creek onto the Skyline Ridge trail.
tags.hand:safety: Long day: watch the last ride down. Snow gets deep in the forest below treeline. Above the trees the ridge meets steep avalanche slopes and cornices.

tags.hand:about: The classic way up Phalanx Mountain (2,441 m) from Blackcomb's backcountry gate, and the way to the top of the Poop Chutes: across the Blackcomb Glacier, up the skin track over the Spearhead's south shoulder, down onto the Spearhead Glacier, a sidehill on the east side of the Spearhead-Phalanx col to the apron under Phalanx's southeast face, then the Stairmaster: a steep, narrow couloir you bootpack to the notch between Phalanx's two summits. From the top, ski down the Phalanx Glacier to the Poop Chutes (their card has the way down).
tags.hand:aka: Stairmaster, Stair master, Stairs master, Stairmaster Couloir, Phalanx Mountain, Phalanx
tags.hand:climb: About 4.2 km and 450 to 500 m of climbing from the top of the Showcase T-Bar to the summit (2 to 2.5 hours); the Stairmaster itself is about 140 m of bootpacking (15 to 20 minutes)
tags.hand:high: 2,441 m (Phalanx's summit); the Stairmaster tops out at about 2,400 m
tags.hand:start: Top of the Showcase T-Bar on Blackcomb (a lift ticket, or skin up from the base), then the backcountry gate on the Blackcomb Glacier into Garibaldi Park.
tags.hand:safety: The Stairmaster is a steep, narrow couloir: an avalanche start zone and a terrain trap, so only on stable days, one at a time, and crampons or an axe help when it's firm. You can't stay on the ridge from the Spearhead to Phalanx: Phalanx's south ridge has rock pinnacles, so sidehill round the east side of the col to the Stairmaster. The north ridge is jagged too: don't follow its crest, ski the Phalanx Glacier beside it. The descent off the Spearhead onto its glacier is steep. In 2021 two size 3 avalanches in the Poop Chutes killed one person.
tags.hand:rules: Past the gate is Garibaldi Provincial Park: nothing is controlled, marked or patrolled.
tags.hand:line: Follows a skier's GPS track from April 2025 (tareef.tech, the link below), simplified. Trip reports from 2010, 2020 and 2023 describe the same way (BCMC, Alpine Baking, sverdina.com).

tags.hand:about: Blackcomb's main uphill route: from the top of the Benchlands Climb up through the forest outside the ski area boundary toward Garibaldi Park. Unmaintained, marked with blue flagging tape. You need to navigate (map, compass, GPS). Check the terrain status map before you come back into the boundary.
tags.hand:rules: All weather conditions route. Unmaintained. Snowshoes allowed. Whistler Blackcomb's rules: uphill travel inside the boundary only on signed routes; carry a transceiver, probe, shovel, skins and a phone (needed to buy a backcountry ticket); sign the Backcountry Access Agreement; routes open and close with the weather and avalanche work, so check the terrain status map the morning you go.

tags.hand:aka: Anniversary Glacier, Anniversary Col, Matier-Joffre col, Cerise Creek
tags.hand:about: The classic glacier tour from Keith's Hut: up through the forest and the ridge behind the hut, past Motel 66, then up the Anniversary Glacier to the col between Mount Matier and Joffre Peak. A wide, open glacier run back down to the hut. Climbers go on from the col to Matier (2,783 m) by its northeast ridge, with ice axes.
tags.hand:climb: About 740 m over 2.7 km one way from the hut (3 to 4 hours up); add the 4 km and 550 m from the road to the hut
tags.hand:aspect: North and northeast (the glacier); the slopes back to the hut face south
tags.hand:start: Keith's Hut (Keith Flavelle Memorial Hut, first come, first served, fee) at about 1,650 m. Reach it on the Keith's Hut Winter Access up Cerise Creek from Highway 99 (Duffey Lake Road), about 4 km and 550 m up from the road (2 hours or so).
tags.hand:safety: Glacier travel: crevasses, sometimes hidden under thin new snow. Steep slopes above the glacier (Matier and Joffre) can avalanche onto it, and the south-facing slopes on the way back to the hut get loose in sun or rain. A huge landslide came off Joffre Peak's northeast face in 2019 and changed the ground below it: check recent trip reports.
tags.hand:line: Drawn from the trip reports and the terrain model (the easiest way from the hut to the col), not a GPS track: follow the skin track and your own judgment.

links.t: Altus Mountain Guides: Duffey Lake area skiing

tags.hand:aka: Vantage, Vantage ridge, Cerise Creek
tags.hand:about: The other day tour from Keith's Hut: up the ridge southeast of the hut to Vantage Peak, with the best view of the Joffre group and the Anniversary Glacier. Lots of climbing for the turns, but unbeatable scenery; the steeper east face is a known line for stable days.
tags.hand:climb: About 630 m over 2.4 km one way from the hut (2 to 3 hours up); add the 4 km and 550 m from the road to the hut
tags.hand:aspect: Northwest (the ridge up); the east face is steep
tags.hand:start: Keith's Hut (Keith Flavelle Memorial Hut, first come, first served, fee) at about 1,650 m. Reach it on the Keith's Hut Winter Access up Cerise Creek from Highway 99 (Duffey Lake Road), about 4 km and 550 m up from the road (2 hours or so).
tags.hand:safety: Corniced ridge: keep back from the edge. The east face is steep avalanche terrain. Slopes off the ridge into Cerise Creek reach 30° and more.
tags.hand:line: Drawn from the trip reports, the summer route and the terrain model, not a GPS track: follow the skin track and your own judgment.

routes.name: Wedgemount Lake (winter way to the hut)

tags.hand:about: The winter way into Wedgemount Lake, under Wedge Mountain (2,892 m, the highest peak in Garibaldi Provincial Park), Mount Weart, Parkhurst and Rethel. Skin up the Wedgemount forest road to its end, cross the creek, then a skin track through the forest (with an open glade) that joins the summer trail and follows it up to the lake. It is not the same as the summer way at the bottom. The top is a steep, rocky gully below the lake; over its crest there is a short run down to the Wedgemount Hut. From the lake, skiers go up the Wedgemount Glacier toward Wedge Mountain and ski the north couloirs of Rethel and the faces between Parkhurst and Rethel.
tags.hand:aka: Wedgemount, Wedgemount Hut, Wedge Mountain, Wedge, Wedgemount Glacier, Rethel, Parkhurst, Weart
tags.hand:climb: About 1,270 m over 6.8 km one way from the road fork at about 640 m to the crest above the hut at about 1,930 m (about 4 hours up with overnight packs; about 1.5 hours of that is the road)
tags.hand:high: About 1,930 m (the crest just above the hut); the hut is at about 1,910 m
tags.hand:start: Wedgemount turnoff from Highway 99, north of Whistler. In winter the road is snowy from the highway: people park at the turnoff or past the bridge, and skin up the forest road (taking the right fork).
tags.hand:safety: The way up crosses an open avalanche slope partway up, and the rocky gully just below the lake is steep, with steeper slopes beside it. Avalanches off Rethel's north face have run all the way to the lake, and large ones come off Wedge's north face. Early in the season the trail can be too thin to skin: one party in December 2023 bootpacked most of it and turned back before the lake. Wedge Mountain itself is glaciated, with an icefall and a corniced ridge.
tags.hand:rules: Wedgemount Lake is in Garibaldi Provincial Park. The Wedgemount Hut is a small BC Parks emergency shelter: check BC Parks for the current rules before you plan to sleep in it, and carry a tent.
tags.hand:line: Follows a skier's GPS track from March 2023 (tareef.tech, the link below), simplified, from the road fork to the hut.

tags.hand:about: A Duffey peak past the Joffre Lakes: up the Joffre Lakes trail and across the lakes to Upper Joffre Lake under Slalok, then up the drainage to the col between Tszil and Taylor. The usual ski route then wraps south around the peak and climbs its western slopes, then goes northwest to the open slopes under the summit block and up the ridge to the summit (2,318 m). Skiers come down the north side.
tags.hand:aka: Taylor, Mt Taylor, Tszil-Taylor col, Joffre Lakes
tags.hand:climb: About 1,090 m over 7.6 km one way (about 5 hours up)
tags.hand:aspect: North and east on the approach, west on the climb; the usual ski descent faces north
tags.hand:start: Joffre Lakes parking on Highway 99 (Duffey Lake Road).
tags.hand:safety: The western slope on the usual ski route is an exposed avalanche slope with a bad runout: on days when it isn't safe to cross, the ridge is the other way. The trail below the lakes crosses an avalanche slope. Corniced col between Tszil and Taylor. The lakes are only crossable when frozen solid (one party turned back on the first lake in April). Big gap at the bottom of a couloir off the summit.
tags.hand:rules: In Joffre Lakes Park (Pipi7íyekw). The park has closed at times for the Lil'wat and N'Quatqua Nations: check BC Parks before you go.
tags.hand:line: Follows a skier's GPS track from April 2025 (tareef.tech, the link below), simplified, up to the summit.

routes.name: Blowdown Peak (from the Blowdown forest road)

tags.hand:about: A Duffey peak east of Duffey Lake: skin up the Blowdown forest road past the junction with the Steep Creek road to its end, then the forest (lower skin track), a boulder field with switchbacks, the drainage toward the col between Blowdown and Crabbe, and the summit plateau. The top is a boulder you scramble up. Melissa's, one of the two big north-facing avalanche paths off the summit ridge, is the known ski line down; skiers traverse hard left at about 1,700 m back to the skin track at the boulder field.
tags.hand:aka: Blowdown, Melissa's, Melissas, Blowdown Creek, Crabbe
tags.hand:climb: About 1,190 m over 7.9 km one way (5 hours or more up; the road alone is about 1 hour 45 minutes)
tags.hand:start: Bottom of the Blowdown forest road off Highway 99 (Duffey Lake Road). You can't park on the forest road in winter: park off it. Sleds use the road.
tags.hand:safety: Melissa's is an avalanche path. The ridge is wind-scoured with rocks under the snow, and there can be rocks hidden under powder lower down. Steep slopes rise above parts of the way up.
tags.hand:line: Follows a skier's GPS track from December 2025 (tareef.tech, the link below), simplified, up to the summit.

tags.hand:about: A big spring day to the high point of the Mamquam Icefield, east of Squamish: up the old Mamquam forest road and the Darling Lake trail, across Paranoid Creek on a log, through forest and two boulder fields to a ridge, then along it to Darling Lake. Past a smaller lake, sidehill round rock outcrops up to the icefield at the pass between Darling Peak and Mamquam, cross the icefield north of Delusion Peak, then bootpack to the summit ridge and the summit (2,588 m). Ski the icefield back to the lake.
tags.hand:aka: Mamquam, Mamquam Icefield, Darling Lake, Delusion Peak
tags.hand:climb: About 1,780 m over 10.6 km one way (about 8 hours up); 22 km and about 1,950 m of climbing return
tags.hand:start: Start of the Mamquam forest road, east of Squamish. Low down the snow is often patchy in spring: expect to carry skis.
tags.hand:safety: Glacier travel on the Mamquam Icefield. Cornices and rime on the ridges; an exposed ramp near the summit where a fall would be serious. Wet slide debris on the sidehill past Darling Lake. A steep slope up to the ridge at about 1,550 m. The Paranoid Creek log is not an official crossing.
tags.hand:rules: Mamquam Mountain is in Garibaldi Provincial Park.
tags.hand:line: Follows a skier's GPS track from April 2025 (tareef.tech, the link below), simplified, up to the summit; the party's dead end on the summit ridge is taken out.

tags.hand:safety: The way in crosses slide paths: don't stop in them. Lakes in the basin: only on thick ice.

tags.hand:about: Long chutes off Phalanx Mountain down to Glacier Road. From the summit (up the Stairmaster), north down the Phalanx Glacier beside the north ridge (not on its crest), a short climb or bootpack west over the lower north ridge (about 40 m, 10 minutes), then down the chutes to Glacier Road. Then Glacier Road to the Crystal or Excelerator chairs, or the valley.
tags.hand:high: 2,441 m (Phalanx's summit); Glacier Road at about 1,650 m
tags.hand:aspect: North (the glacier), then west and northwest (the chutes)
tags.hand:start: Phalanx's summit, from the Stairmaster (see "Phalanx Mountain via the Stairmaster").
tags.hand:safety: Don't ski the north ridge's crest: it's jagged. The chutes are long and narrow and funnel any slide: in 2021 two size 3 avalanches here killed one person. The lower chutes (the dogleg) can be icy above a cliff. Go past the bench and you end up in the Wedge Creek drainage, a long way from the ski area. Glacier: crevasses.
tags.hand:rules: Garibaldi Provincial Park: nothing is controlled, marked or patrolled until you're back on Glacier Road.
tags.hand:line: Redrawn from a skier's GPS track from April 2025 (tareef.tech), simplified: the only public GPS track of this descent found. OpenStreetMap's line starts on the north ridge's crest; a 2023 trip report (sverdina.com) also says they went along the ridge to a drop-in, but no GPS track shows it.
